pipeline_steps.description: Median imputation for numerical features; mode imputation for categorical features.
OneHotEncoding for categorical; StandardScaler for numerical.
Linear dimensionality reduction to 6 orthogonal components.
Feature bounding into [0, π] domain for angle and ZZFeatureMap parameter binding.

evidence.verdict_explanation: Under the selected experimental configuration, classical models show higher observed ROC-AUC than VQC (best classical 0.921 vs. VQC 0.492; delta: -0.428). This is an observational result on the evaluated dataset and configuration.

performance_evidence.description: Best classical baseline shows a higher observed ROC-AUC than VQC under the evaluation protocol (0.921 ± 0.066 vs. VQC 0.492 ± 0.199; delta: -0.428).

generalization_evidence.description: VQC shows higher observed fold-to-fold variance than the classical baseline (VQC SD: ±0.199 vs. Classical SD: ±0.066). This may indicate higher sensitivity to data partitioning.

calibration_evidence.description: Classical model shows better observed calibration accuracy (Classical Brier: 0.116 ± 0.035 vs. VQC Brier: 0.262 ± 0.028).

robustness_evidence.description: VQC retains 112.9% of ideal ROC-AUC under simulated noise (Noisy AUC: 0.556, Ideal AUC: 0.492). Noise simulation mode: UNKNOWN.

resource_evidence.description: Quantum simulation runtime is 162.6× higher than classical inference (31.38 ms vs. 0.19 ms). This reflects classical simulation overhead, not future hardware timing.

rule_breakdown: Classical baselines show higher observed ROC-AUC (delta: -0.428)
evidence.methodological_note: Conclusions are observational and based on held-out test and cross-validation metrics. No formal statistical significance test has been applied. Do not interpret metric differences as statistically significant without appropriate hypothesis testing (e.g., DeLong test, bootstrap).

logistic_regression.method_description: Logistic Regression coefficients represent the log-odds change per unit increase in each standardized input feature.  The absolute magnitude indicates relative influence on the linear decision boundary. Sign (positive/negative) indicates direction of association. This interpretation applies only to the fitted linear model.
logistic_regression.interpretation_note: Values are absolute coefficient magnitudes from the fitted Logistic Regression model on the PCA-compressed held-out feature space. They reflect the model's internal weighting, not causal clinical importance.

random_forest.method_description: Random Forest impurity-based feature importance measures the mean decrease in Gini impurity weighted by the fraction of samples reaching each split node, averaged across all trees in the ensemble. Scores are normalized to sum to 1.0. This is a training-data measure and may over-weight high-cardinality or correlated features.
random_forest.interpretation_note: Impurity-based importance is computed from the fitted Random Forest on the PCA-compressed training data. It reflects tree-split utility, not causal clinical relevance.

svm.method_description: Permutation importance is a model-agnostic method that measures the mean ROC-AUC decrease when each feature's values are randomly permuted across the held-out test set (5 repetitions, random seed 42). A larger drop indicates that the model relies more heavily on that feature for discrimination. Negative values are clipped to zero.
svm.interpretation_note: Permutation importance is evaluated on the held-out test split. It reflects the model's dependence on each feature but is not a causal attribution.

vqc.method_description: Measures the average rate of change in VQC positive-class probability with respect to ±0.05-step perturbations in each quantum-encoded feature (PCA component).  This is a local sensitivity measure, NOT a SHAP value, NOT a gradient, and NOT a causal attribution. Higher sensitivity means the circuit output is more responsive to changes in that encoded dimension.

quantum_sensitivity.methodology: Finite-difference sensitivity: sensitivity_j = mean_i |P(+|x+δej) − P(+|x−δej)| / 2δ (δ=0.05, 16 test samples). Back-projection to original features uses |PCA loading| weighted sum.

vqc.interpretation_note: Quantum Feature Sensitivity is computed via finite-difference perturbation of the parameterized quantum circuit inputs.  It reflects circuit-output sensitivity, not causal clinical feature importance.

quantum_resources.simulator_backend: Qiskit Aer Statevector / Depolarizing Noise Simulator

classical_resources.parameter_count_summary: RBF Kernel Support Vectors (~24 support vectors)

resource_profile.measured_vs_configured_notes: Circuit depth (5) and parameter count (18) are exact analytical circuit properties. Simulation time (9.725s) and latencies (31.38ms) are empirical CPU runtime measurements on local Python/Qiskit execution.
resource_profile.scalability_disclaimer: Observed resource metrics are measured on local CPU statevector / Aer simulation. Physical quantum execution on fault-tolerant hardware exhibits distinct asymptotic scaling, circuit compilation overhead, and error mitigation budgets.
